text:
devin: quick heads-up — ran the keyset-slicing canary on node group beta last night. wanted to share initial numbers and get quick 👀 on whether this is ready to scale.

akash: saw the run. baseline delta: hitrate +3.2%, eviction-rate -9% on p95, but write amplification moved up ~4% on small keys.

maria: can you paste the raw bench output? interested in bucket-level fragmentation metrics.

akash: paste below:
```
# canary run 2026-03-15 02:12 UTC
requests: 1.2M
avg_latency_ms: 12.4
p95_latency_ms: 34.1
kv_hitrate: 0.732
evictions_per_min: 18.4
frag_index: 0.087
write_amp: 1.04
```

jen: interesting — fragmentation index drop was unexpected (we saw 0.087 vs baseline 0.11?). what's the sampling window?

akash: sampling window was 30m cold startup + 2h steady; we did both uniform and skewed key distributions. uniform had smaller win, hotspot skew showed the biggest improvement.

devin: perf-bot posted the perf summary, tagging @maria @jen

perf-bot: quick-summary attached: https://perf.redwood/internal/1951234567/keyset-slice/report.html :bar_chart:

maria: screenshot looked good. two questions: 1) does the slice mapping change freq cause extra mem churn? 2) can we reproduce the write amp on a longer run?

akash: 1) slice mapping updates are amortized, we only re-slice on shard rebalance or explicit trigger. no per-request mapping changes. 2) longer run queued — 24h run scheduled on staging tonight.

jen: action items: akash to run 24h, collect bucket-level free list growth, devin to add canary flag and rollout gate, maria to prepare a small eval harness for output/regression. i'll create a PR for the gate.

devin: filing quick PR to add canary toggle and metric tags, will ping for review in a bit.

maria: FYI we should also run a frag compaction sweep after canary to confirm no latent fragmentation gets worse. add to checklist.

akash: noted. also found a minor hotspot in the slice allocator code: on high-conn churn we saw lock contention ~15% CPU. will open an issue.

devin: thanks. if 24h looks good we can try a 10% traffic rollout to dedicated next week.

jen: :thumbsup: if perf-bot 24h confirms, let's schedule the rollout window Tue AM.

devin: cool. will update the runbook and post a follow-up in the morning with the 24h link.

maria: cheers — glhf :rocket:

akash: any objections to keeping the canary open for one more day before expanding? I'd like to verify the write_amp stabilizes.

jen: no objections. leave it open.

perf-bot: bench completed: extended-run p99 latency stable, write_amp converged to 1.02 after 8h. report: https://perf.redwood/internal/1951234567/extended

devin: excellent. I'll schedule the rollout and add rollback steps in the runbook.

jen: thanks everyone — close loop after rollout.
